definitions.explanation: Traditional Japanese poetry, especially the 31-syllable tanka form (5-7-5-7-7), distinguished from Chinese poetry.

examples.japanese: ⟦{万葉集|まんようしゅう}→万葉集：08827_manyoushuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{多|おお}く→多く：18752_ooku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{和歌|わか}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{収|おさ}められている→収める：02022_osameru⟧。
examples.english: The Man'yoshu contains many waka poems.

examples.japanese: ⟦{平安|へいあん}→平安：12641_heian⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{和歌|わか}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{盛|さか}ん→盛ん：01239_sakan⟧⟦だった→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Waka poetry flourished in the Heian period.

notes:
{和歌|わか} literally means 'Japanese song/poem' ({和|わ} = Japanese, {歌|か} = song). It refers to traditional Japanese poetry as distinct from ⟦{漢詩|かんし}→漢詩：13438_kanshi⟧ (Chinese poetry).

FORMS:
- ⟦{短歌|たんか}→短歌：15358_tanka⟧ (5-7-5-7-7): the most common form, often simply called {和歌|わか}
- ⟦{長歌|ちょうか}→長歌：noentry⟧: longer poems with alternating 5-7 mora patterns

FAMOUS COLLECTIONS:
- ⟦{万葉集|まんようしゅう}→万葉集：08827_manyoushuu⟧: oldest anthology (8th century)
- ⟦{古今和歌集|こきんわかしゅう}→古今和歌集：noentry⟧: compiled 905 CE
- ⟦{百人一首|ひゃくにんいっしゅ}→百人一首：22329_hyakuninisshu⟧: 100 famous poems, still used in card games

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {和歌|わか}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詠|よ}む→詠む：14186_yomu⟧: to compose a waka poem
- {和歌|わか}⟦{集|しゅう}→集：noentry⟧: waka anthology

Note: ⟦{俳句|はいく}→俳句：00083_haiku⟧ (haiku, 5-7-5) developed later as a separate genre and is not classified as {和歌|わか}.
